1.explanation: src/core/run/r.ts is where Quarto’s R engine takes the plain text output of pander() and wraps it as a RawBlock("markdown", …). Because that RawBlock is later placed inside a Div cell-output-display, Pandoc indents every line by two spaces when it writes Markdown, turning what should be a flat list into a nested one. src/format/markdown/format-markdown.ts is Pandoc’s Markdown writer; it governs how blocks (including RawBlocks inside Divs) are indented and emitted. Finally, resources/filters/quarto-post/cellcleanup.lua is the Lua filter that post-processes code-cell output and could strip or flatten the Div around the raw Markdown. A fix will involve changing r.ts so that raw Markdown list blocks are not wrapped in a container that triggers indenting, adjusting format-markdown.ts so that RawBlocks inside certain Pandoc Divs are not indented, or updating cellcleanup.lua to remove or flatten the enclosing Div before Pandoc writes out the Markdown.
1.bug_scenario: When you call pander::pander(list("1","2",3,c(1,2))) inside a Quarto (.qmd) document, Quarto’s R‐engine emits raw Markdown for the list but wraps it in a Div with class {.cell-output-display}. That wrapper causes Pandoc’s Markdown writer to indent everything by two spaces, so only the first "* 1" is a top‐level bullet and the rest become nested bullets (sub-points) rather than all four items being at the same level.

2.explanation: In src/execute/markdown.ts you’ll find the helper that formats cell output (cellOutputDisplay, cellOutputError, etc.), and it applies a two-space indent to every line of stdout. In src/execute/qmd.ts these helpers are used to wrap R chunk output in a ::: {.cell-output-display} block. The extra leading spaces turn pander’s top-level '*' markers into nested list items. Removing or adjusting that indent logic will restore the correct flat bullet list.
2.bug_scenario: When you run a little QMD document that calls pander::pander(list("1","2",3,c(1,2))) under Quarto’s built-in engine, the intermediate Markdown comes out wrapped in a Div and every output line is prefixed by two spaces. A pander list that should render as four top-level bullets instead gets its second, third and fourth items indented and rendered as sub-bullets. Knit the same code with knitr::knit() and you see the correct flat list, so the culprit is Quarto’s QMD–execution boilerplate that wraps and indents output.
